clue.text: Tom maybe goes around nude nightclub

indicators.note: the tomcat's letters go around the word for nude, enclosing it

parts.note: a tom is a male cat, given by example
nude and bare both mean unclothed

explanation.surface: A tomcat wanders past a strip club, or a man called Tom heads off to one with nothing on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' looks like a man's name; with 'maybe' it is an example of a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabaret is a venue offering entertainment such as singing and dancing while patrons drink, a kind of nightclub.

clue.text: Scoundrel that is holding diamonds? This person holds clubs

indicators.note: the scoundrel and the abbreviation for that is hold the card suit between them

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A rogue clutching jewels, then a golfer's helper carrying the bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clubs' and 'diamonds' pose as card suits; only diamonds is one, and the clubs are golf clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A caddie carries a golfer's bag of clubs round the course.

clue.text: Capital earned, banked by leaders in Bank of America

indicators.note: flanked on both sides, like a river between banks, so the leading letters go round
the leaders are the first letters of each word

parts.note: the three words whose first letters are taken
got means received or earned

explanation.surface: Money earned is deposited with a major American bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money in this banking scene; it is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Bogotá is the capital city of Colombia.

clue.text: Eccentric avoids more films like Thelma and Louise

indicators.note: eccentric means odd, off-centre, so the letters are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An oddball keeps away from further films of the Thelma and Louise kind.
explanation.walkthrough: Thelma and Louise (1991) follows two women on the run across America by car.
explanation.definitionFit: A road movie is a film whose story unfolds on a journey, typically by car.

clue.text: Bound to include length, like many roofs and bathroom walls

definitions.text: like many roofs and bathroom walls

indicators.note: the word for bound takes in the abbreviation for length

parts.note: bound means tied up

explanation.surface: A builder is obliged to measure length when covering roofs and bathroom walls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to' reads as 'certain to'; Bound alone is the word for tied.
explanation.definitionFit: Roofs and bathroom walls are commonly covered in tiles, so they are tiled.

clue.text: Characters in Toulouse go miles westwards in French city

indicators.note: in an across clue westwards means right to left, so the hidden run is read backwards
the answer is made of letters sitting inside the phrase Toulouse go miles

parts.note: the phrase holding the hidden letters, spanning its last two words

explanation.surface: A traveller in Toulouse drives many miles west to reach another French city.
explanation.walkthrough: The string runs backwards across 'Toulouse go miles', from the end of Toulouse into miles.
explanation.definitionFit: Limoges is a city in west-central France, famous for its porcelain.

clue.text: Get more cheerful GP, until he explodes

indicators.note: an explosion blows the letters apart, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone is told to cheer up before the family doctor loses his temper.
explanation.walkthrough: A GP, general practitioner, is a family doctor in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To lighten up is an idiom for relaxing and becoming less serious or gloomy.

clue.text: M&S clothing really upset supermodel

indicators.note: the store's initials clothe, or surround, the other letters

parts.note: taken as the letters M and S

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the word upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: so means really, as in I'm so tired

explanation.surface: A famous model is truly unhappy at being dressed by Marks and Spencer.
explanation.walkthrough: M&S is Marks and Spencer, a British department store famous for clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Kate Moss is an English supermodel, famous since the 1990s.

clue.text: Jokes about boy king's fine attire

indicators.note: the word for jokes goes about, surrounding, the other pieces

parts.note: gags are jokes
a lad is a boy
R, for rex, is king; the 's is is, a link

explanation.surface: Wisecracks are made about a young king's splendid clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad rags is an informal idiom for one's best clothes, worn for a special occasion.

clue.text: Perhaps some dope from Dorset is confused

definitions.note: dope is drugs; perhaps marks these as an example

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A puzzled idiot from Dorset, an English county, is muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' suggests a fool from Dorset; it is drugs, especially those used to enhance performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Steroids are performance-enhancing drugs, the kind of dope athletes are tested for.

clue.text: It's uncritically believed she's given birth to pups?

definitions.note: a description standing for the noun: the thing that is believed without question

parts.note: a dog is the animal that has pups
a mother, informally ma, is she who has given birth

explanation.surface: A light joke about a dog who has just had a litter of pups.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as DOG MA, the answer is a mother dog, the one who gave birth to pups.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogma is a set of principles laid down by an authority and accepted without question.

clue.text: Liberal, for example, is behind what MPs do

parts.note: taken as written
behind as in behind schedule, which is late

explanation.surface: A Liberal MP trails the others in some parliamentary task.
explanation.walkthrough: MPs are Members of Parliament in Britain, whose job is to make laws.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of Parliament pass laws, which is to legislate, the core business of a parliament.

clue.text: Bully Henman, say, interrupts during one tryst

indicators.note: the tennis player's first name breaks into the run of the other pieces

parts.note: in means during, as in in the night
a tryst is a romantic meeting, a date
Tim Henman, the British tennis player, is an example of a Tim

explanation.surface: The tennis player Henman barges in on someone's romantic meeting and spoils it.
explanation.walkthrough: Tim Henman was a much-loved British tennis player of the 1990s and 2000s.
explanation.definitionFit: To bully someone is to frighten them into submission, which is to intimidate them.

clue.text: Liveliness in British carnival location

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro hosts the world's most famous carnival

explanation.surface: There is plenty of energy at a carnival held somewhere in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Brio is vigour or vivacity of style, the same idea as liveliness.

clue.text: Violent winds are able to break rushes

indicators.note: the word for are able breaks into the word for rushes

parts.note: to rush is to hurry
can means are able

explanation.surface: Fierce gales can flatten the reeds growing by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rushes' looks like waterside plants that the wind might flatten; here it is the verb meaning hurries.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurricanes are tropical storms with extremely strong winds.

clue.text: Drinking litres, drunk devoured gin and had a binge

indicators.note: the jumbled letters take in, or drink, the abbreviation for litres
drunk means the letters of devoured gin are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone sinks litres of drink and wolfs down gin in one long session.
explanation.definitionFit: To overindulge is to have too much of something, and a binge is a bout of excess.

clue.text: Actor Oliver, you heard, with Ms Blanchett in train again

parts.note: Oliver Reed was an English film actor

indicators.note: heard signals that the word you is taken by its sound, as a single letter

parts.note: the word whose sound gives a single letter
Cate Blanchett is an Australian actress

explanation.surface: Two film stars, Oliver Reed and Cate Blanchett, appear together on a train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' looks like a railway train carrying the actors; it is the verb to teach.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-educate is to teach someone again, often to change their ideas or skills.

clue.text: Beating court card at the end of bridge

indicators.note: the card's name is placed after the word for bridge

parts.note: a span is a bridge or the arch of one
the king is a court card, along with queen and jack

explanation.surface: Taking a trick with a picture card at the close of a game of bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bridge' looks like the card game, fitting 'court card'; here it is a structure over a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A spanking is a beating, typically a smack on the bottom.

clue.text: Laugh over epic poet's Broadway musical

indicators.note: in a down clue the laugh sits over, above, the poet's name

parts.note: ha is a laugh
John Milton wrote the epic Paradise Lost; the 's is is, a link

explanation.surface: A poet of epics laughing at a Broadway show.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamilton is Lin-Manuel Miranda's hit hip-hop stage show about Alexander Hamilton.

clue.text: People preventing conflict in games with great goalies

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school games
ace means excellent, great
goalkeepers are keepers

explanation.surface: A sports team relies on excellent goalkeepers in its matches.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools, games and PE are both names for the sports lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: Peacekeepers are forces sent to stop fighting breaking out between sides.

clue.text: Strange case for hearty cops in chilling film

indicators.note: strange means odd, so these letters are put into an odd order
the case of a word is its outer letters, first and last

parts.note: the word whose outer letters are taken
taken as written

explanation.surface: An odd crime story about cheerful police officers in a frightening movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Psycho is Alfred Hitchcock's 1960 horror thriller, famous for its shower scene.

clue.text: Fools receiving tons in benefits

indicators.note: the word for fools receives, taking inside it, the abbreviation for tons

parts.note: asses are fools

explanation.surface: Idiots are said to be raking in huge sums in welfare payments.
explanation.definitionFit: Assets are advantages or useful qualities, things that benefit someone.

clue.text: Catch tails of lion, zebra, okapi and jackal

indicators.note: the tail of each animal's name is its final letter

parts.note: the three animals whose final letters are taken
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tries to grab the tails of a menagerie of African animals.
explanation.definitionFit: To nail a criminal is to catch or pin them down, a common informal sense.

clue.text: Alehouse enumerates about 101 advertisers

parts.note: an alehouse is a pub

indicators.note: the word for enumerates goes about, surrounding, the Roman number

parts.note: to enumerate is to list things one by one
CI is 101 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A pub's landlord counts off around a hundred and one marketing people.
explanation.definitionFit: Publicists promote people or products in the press, the job of advertisers.

clue.text: Compare Elvis regularly with Barbie's beau

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals, here every second one

parts.note: the name whose alternate letters are taken
Ken is the boyfriend doll of Barbie

explanation.surface: Someone sets Elvis side by side with Barbie's boyfriend Ken.
explanation.definitionFit: To liken one thing to another is to compare them or point out a similarity.

clue.text: I was first, turning up in food shop

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up reads the letters from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: taken as written
to lead is to be first, so was first is led

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of being first to arrive at the grocer's.
explanation.definitionFit: A deli, short for delicatessen, is a shop selling prepared and speciality foods.

clue.text: Not knowing where Noah was, around end of flood

indicators.note: the phrase for Noah's whereabouts is placed around the final letter

parts.note: Noah rode out the flood in the ark

indicators.note: the end of flood is its last letter

parts.note: the word whose final letter is taken

explanation.surface: A puzzled thought about where Noah spent the time as the flood ended.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the dark is an idiom for being uninformed or ignorant of something.

clue.text: Our monarch in new coat of attractive, shiny material

indicators.note: the monarch's letters sit inside the outer letters of the next word
the coat of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

parts.note: the word whose outer letters, its coat, are taken
CR, Carolus Rex, is King Charles, the current British monarch

explanation.surface: The King appears in a new and attractive coat made of glossy stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: CR stands for Carolus Rex, Latin for King Charles.
explanation.definitionFit: Nacre is mother-of-pearl, the iridescent substance lining some shells.

clue.text: Real ingenue moving in

indicators.note: the letters of ingenue are moved around into a new order

parts.note: an ingenue is an innocent young woman; here just its letters are used

explanation.surface: An innocent young woman really is moving in, perhaps with a new flatmate.
explanation.definitionFit: Genuine means authentic, truly what it seems, a synonym of real.

clue.text: People who don't appear in casinos — how silly!

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters across these words

parts.note: the phrase containing the answer, from the end of casinos to the start of silly

explanation.definitionFit: A no-show is someone who books or is expected but fails to turn up.
